extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on drafting and handling Office actions, applying rejections, avoiding piecemeal examination, and processing petitions to make applications special (including accelerated examination). Primarily aimed at USPTO examiners but also relevant to applicants and their representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: General Allegation of Patentability (¶7.37.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant’s arguments fail to comply with 37 CFR 1.111(b) because they amount to a general allegation that the claims define a patentable invention without specifically pointing out how the language of the claims patentably distinguishes them from the references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.37. Briefly restate the recitation about which applicant is arguing (insert in bracket 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Novelty Not Clearly Pointed Out (¶7.37.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant’s arguments do not comply with 37 CFR 1.111(c) because they do not clearly point out the patentable novelty which he or she thinks the claims present in view of the state of the art disclosed by the references cited or the objections made, nor show how the amendments avoid such references or objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Arguing Against References Individually (¶7.37.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: When rejections are based on combinations of references, one cannot show nonobviousness by attacking references individually (see In re Keller; In re Merck & Co.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of Piecemeal Examination (707.07(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Piecemeal examination should be avoided where possible; the examiner ordinarily should reject each claim on all valid grounds available, avoiding undue multiplication of references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major technical rejections (lack of proper disclosure, lack of enablement, serious indefiniteness, res judicata) should be applied where appropriate and stated with full development of reasons rather than by mere conclusion. Where prior art discloses the 'heart' of the invention, secondary rejections on minor technical grounds should ordinarily not be made. Certain technical rejections (e.g., negative limitations, indefiniteness) should not be made where the examiner is not aware of an improved mode of definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations Permitting Limited Action on Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Some situations justify limiting action on claims to a particular issue rather than full action on merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: (A) application too informal for complete action (see MPEP §702.01); (B) undue multiplicity of claims with no successful election request (see MPEP §2173.05(n)); (C) misjoinder of inventions with no successful election (see MPEP §803, §810, §812.01); (D) disclosure directed to perpetual motion (cite Ex parte Payne) — in such cases cite best prior art without specifically applying it to the claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify of Inaccuracies in Amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: When amendments contain inaccuracies, the examiner should notify (see MPEP §714.23).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference to MPEP §714.23 for detailed procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each Claim To Be Mentioned in Each Office Action (707.07(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: In every Office action, each pending claim should be mentioned by number, and its treatment or status given; include a summary of the status of all claims presented for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTO-326 'Office Action Summary' should be used. Keep the Index of Claims up to date as set forth in MPEP §719.04. For Image File Wrapper (IFW) processing, see IFW Manual. Treat claims retained under 37 CFR 1.142 and 1.146 as set out in MPEP §821 to §821.04(b). See MPEP Chapter 2300 for interfering party claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: State When Claims Are Allowable (707.07(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: When the application discloses patentable subject matter but claims cannot be allowed due to defects in form or omission of a limitation, the examiner should be constructive and offer definite suggestions for correction and may indicate desirability of an interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If aspects of patentable invention are not claimed but appear in the disclosure, note that if properly claimed such claims may receive favorable consideration. If a claim is otherwise allowable but dependent on a canceled or rejected claim, state it would be allowable if rewritten in independent form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early Allowance of Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the examiner is satisfied that the prior art has been fully developed and some claims are clearly allowable, allowance of such claims should not be delayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs 7.43, 7.43.01, and 7.43.02 may be used to indicate allowable subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable Subject Matter — 35 U.S.C. 112, Second Paragraph (¶7.43.01 & ¶7.43.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] would be allowable if rewritten or amended to overcome the rejection(s) under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, set forth in this Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ¶7.43.01 when noted independent or dependent claims are rejected solely on the basis of 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph. Use ¶7.43.02 for dependent claims to include all limitations of the base claim and intervening claims. Examiner notes explain when each is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggestion of Allowable Drafted Claim(s), Pro Se (¶7.43.04)
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may draft and present a suggested claim considered to distinguish patentably over the art of record to pro se applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the suggested claim is not embraced by the original oath or declaration, require a supplemental oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.67. Insert complete text of suggested claim(s) in bracket 3. Form paragraph 7.97 may be used to indicate allowance of claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Allowed (¶7.97)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate when claim(s) are allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ¶7.97 with appropriate insertion of allowed claim numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objection to Claims — Allowable Subject Matter / Numbering Paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.description: If a claim is objected to as being dependent upon a rejected base claim but would be allowable if rewritten in independent form including all limitations, state so; number paragraphs of the Office action consecutively to facilitate identification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good practice to number paragraphs consecutively for traceability in prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment on Examples and Test Results (707.07(l))
rubrics_metrics.description: The results of tests and examples should not normally be questioned by the examiner unless there is reasonable basis for questioning the results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner questions results, the appropriate claims should be rejected as based on insufficient disclosure under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph (see In re Borkowski). Applicant must reply, e.g., by providing results of an actual test or relevant arguments. Care should be taken not to enter new matter. If questions as to operability or utility are present, consider applicability of a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 101. See MPEP §§2161-2164.08(c) and §706.03(a), §2107 et seq.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing and Initialing by Assistant Examiner (707.08)
rubrics_metrics.description: The full surname of the examiner who prepares the Office action must be typed at the end of the action; the telephone number below should be called if the application is to be discussed or an interview arranged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraphs 7.100, 7.101 or 7.102 at the conclusion of all actions. The preparer should initial and, if not authorized to sign, forward to the authorized signatory for signing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone Inquiry Contact Form Paragraphs (¶7.100–7.102)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide contact name and telephone number for inquiries concerning the communication; specify days and duty hours, and supervisor contact if attempts are unsuccessful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fill bracket fields appropriately (name, area code & phone number, work days, duty hours, SPE name and phone). Include PAIR access information and EBC contact for Private PAIR access questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Returned Office Action Procedures (707.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Office actions are returned by USPS, technical support staff should check whether mailed to correct correspondence address; if not, remail and stamp 'remailed' with remailing date; period running against application begins with remailing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If mailed to correct address and addressed to an attorney/agent, write inventor/assignee informing of returned action. If undeliverable and remailing fails, place action and envelope in file wrapper; for IFW, add copy of letter and envelope. If the remailing period elapses with no communication from applicant, the application is abandoned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of Examination (708)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonprovisional applications accepted as complete are assigned to Technology Centers and taken up for examination in the order filed except for those advanced pursuant to 37 CFR 1.102; examiner ordinarily gives priority to application in docket with the oldest effective U.S. filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain exceptions: international national stage order per 37 CFR 1.496 and MPEP §1893.03; priority to reissue applications, reexaminations involved in litigation, special cases with fixed due dates. Amendments before final rejection should be responded to within two months.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of Special Cases (708.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifies cases to be advanced out of turn for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes (A) inventions of peculiar importance requested by government department head; (B) made special by petition; (C) reissues in stayed litigation; (D) applications remanded by appellate tribunal; (E) cases transferred but previously taken up; (F) applications appearing to interfere; (G) ready for allowance; (H) in condition for final rejection; (I) pending more than 5 years; (J) reexamination proceedings. See §708.01 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition To Make Special — General Conditions (708.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications will not be advanced out of turn except as provided or upon order of the Director or upon filing a request or petition under specified paragraphs; any statement in support must be based on a good faith belief that the invention qualifies for special status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain petitions are without fee (e.g., applicant's age or health, environmental quality, energy, countering terrorism). Other petitions require fee per 37 CFR 1.17(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition To Make Special — Manufacture (I)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application may be made special on the ground of prospective manufacture upon filing a petition with fee and a statement alleging possession of sufficient currently available capital and facilities to manufacture in quantity or that such will be made available if patent granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional requirements: (A) if prospective manufacturer is an individual, corroborating bank/officer statement; (B) statement that manufacturer will not manufacture or increase manufacture unless patent is certain; (C) obligation to manufacture in the United States or possessions upon allowance; (D) that applicant/assignee has made a careful and thorough search of prior art or has good knowledge thereof. Applicant must provide copies of closest references if not of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition To Make Special — Infringement (II)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application may be made special for actual (not prospective) infringement upon payment of fee and statement alleging an infringing device/product on the market or method in use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement must attest that a rigid comparison with the claims shows some claims unquestionably infringed and that a careful prior art search was made. Applicant must provide copies of the most closely related references if not of record. Models/specimens should not be submitted unless requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition To Make Special — Applicant’s Health/Age (III & IV)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be made special without fee if applicant's health or 65+ age is demonstrated by appropriate evidence (doctor's certificate, birth certificate, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal/medical information submitted will be available to the public if the application file is public (37 CFR 1.11 or 1.14); if applicant does not wish this, submit information pursuant to MPEP §724.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition To Make Special — Environmental Quality (V)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will accord 'special' status to patent applications for inventions which materially enhance the quality of the environment by contributing to the restoration or maintenance of air, water, or soil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition under 37 CFR 1.102 must state that special status is sought for this reason; no fee required. If disclosure does not clearly show material enhancement, petition must be accompanied by a statement explaining how the materiality standard is met. Materiality cannot be speculative or based on hypothetical end-user applications; minor aspects are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition To Make Special — Energy (VI)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will accord 'special' status to applications for inventions which materially contribute to (A) discovery/development of energy resources or (B) more efficient utilization and conservation of energy resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include fossil fuels, hydrogen fuel, nuclear, solar, or inventions reducing energy consumption. Petition must state which category is claimed; no fee if clear on face (37 CFR 1.102(c)). If not clear, petition must be accompanied by a statement explaining how materiality is met. Materiality cannot be speculative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition To Make Special — Recombinant DNA (VII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Special status will be accorded to patent applications relating to safety of research in recombinant DNA upon appropriate petition and payment of fee under 37 CFR 1.17(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition should be accompanied by statements explaining the relationship of the invention to safety of recombinant DNA research. See NIH 'Guidelines for Research Involving Recombinant DNA Molecules' and related Federal Register materials for context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Examining Procedure — Accelerated Examination (VIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: A new application may be granted special (accelerated) status provided applicant complies with each of the required items for accelerated examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At minimum, applicant must submit a petition to make special accompanied by the fee under 37 CFR 1.17(h). Additional required items (search statement, IDS, explanation of relevance, etc.) follow in subsequent provisions (not included in this chunk).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner Assistance to Pro Se Applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: When it becomes apparent during examination that there is patentable subject matter disclosed in a pro se application, the examiner should draft one or more claims for the applicant and indicate that such claims would be allowed if incorporated by amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This practice expedites prosecution and offers service to individual inventors unfamiliar with preparation and prosecution. It is expected to be applied in all cases where applicant is unfamiliar with proper preparation and prosecution and where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major Technical Rejections Must Be Fully Developed
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a major technical rejection is proper (e.g., res judicata, new matter, no prima facie showing for reissue, inoperativeness), it should be accompanied by rejection on all other available grounds and stated with a full development of reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid merely concluding; provide full explanation and reasoning instead of stereotyped expressions. See MPEP §904.03 for undue multiplication of references guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of Claims Retained Under 37 CFR 1.142 and 1.146
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims retained under 37 CFR 1.142 and 1.146 should be treated as set out in MPEP §821 to §821.04(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Chapter 2300 for treatment of losing party claims in interference and IFW Manual for processing.
